mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 0.5% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below a 12-month moving average triggers a negative demand shock, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals weakening consumer and business confidence, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.8% for three consecutive months indicates a broad-based supply contraction, which raises input costs and lowers profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.8% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during three-month INDPRO declines exceeding -0.8%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate above 5% triggers market expectations of prolonged restrictive policy, which increases risk-free rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS jumps above 5% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5% in a single month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in real personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth > 0.4% monthly) and a surge in retail sales (implied by RSAFS growth > 1% monthly) signals a robust demand expansion, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.4% AND RSAFS > 1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during months with PAYEMS > 0.4% and RSAFS > 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent fall in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for three consecutive months, combined with rising average hourly earnings (implied by labor market tightness), signals wage inflation and potential future monetary tightening, which leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as markets anticipate higher corporate pricing power.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during three-month stretches where UNRATE is below 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average, sustained for four consecutive months, signals a housing market recovery that boosts construction-related earnings and consumer confidence, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during four-month stretches where HOUST exceeds its 12-month moving average.
